title: Molecular Dynamics Viewer with Dynamic Difficulty
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a molecular dynamics visualization viewer using Three.js. The scene features a central 3D model loaded from 'Corset.glb' using GLTFLoader (representing a complex molecular structure), surrounded by dynamically simulated particle atoms.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a dark background (0x0a0a1a) with ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.5) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 1.0) at position (5, 10, 5).
- Load 'Corset.glb' using GLTFLoader from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js'. Center the model at (0, 0, 0) and scale it to fit within a 3-unit bounding sphere. This model represents the central molecular scaffold.
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0, 3, 8), looking at origin. Add OrbitControls.
- Generate 30 particle spheres (radius 0.1) orbiting the central model. Each particle has randomized orbital radius (2-5 units), speed, and color based on 'element type' (red=oxygen, blue=nitrogen, green=carbon, white=hydrogen — assign randomly).

PHYSICS / SIMULATION:
- Particles orbit the center with simple circular/elliptical motion. Each particle has properties: position, velocity, orbitalRadius, speed, elementType.
- Implement a 'temperature' variable (range 0.1 to 3.0, default 1.0) that scales particle speeds.
- Implement a 'difficulty' system with 3 levels: Easy (30 particles, slow), Medium (60 particles, medium speed), Hard (90 particles, fast speed + particle trails).
- When difficulty changes, smoothly add/remove particles over 1 second.

DYNAMIC DIFFICULTY:
- Track a 'focus score' (0-100): it increases by 1 every second the user is NOT interacting (idle), decreases by 5 every time the user clicks a particle. If focus score > 70, auto-increase difficulty. If focus score < 30, auto-decrease difficulty.

USER INTERACTIONS:
- Click on a particle (raycasting) to select it. Selected particle glows (emissive 0xffff00) and its info appears in a HUD panel.
- Press 'T' to toggle temperature slider visibility.
- A temperature slider (HTML range input, id='tempSlider') controls the temperature from 0.1 to 3.0.
- Press 'Space' to pause/resume the simulation.
- Press 'D' to manually cycle difficulty (Easy -> Medium -> Hard -> Easy).
- Press 'R' to reset all particles to initial positions and reset focus score to 50.

HUD / UI:
- Top-left: DOM div (id='hud') showing: current difficulty level, particle count, temperature, focus score, simulation status (running/paused).
- Bottom-center: temperature slider (id='tempSlider') with label, hidden by default.
- When a particle is selected, show a panel (id='particleInfo') at top-right with: element type, orbital radius, current speed.

STATE MANAGEMENT (window.__3D_STATE__):
- modelLoaded: boolean, true when Corset.glb is loaded
- particleCount: number of active particles
- temperature: current temperature value
- difficulty: string 'easy'|'medium'|'hard'
- difficultyLevel: number 1|2|3
- focusScore: current focus score (0-100)
- isPaused: boolean
- selectedParticle: null or object {elementType, orbitalRadius, speed}
- simTime: elapsed simulation time in seconds
- sliderVisible: boolean for temperature slider visibility
- particlePositionsValid: boolean, true if no particle has NaN coordinates
- meanOrbitalRadius: average orbital radius of all particles
physics_constraints: Particles must orbit with speeds proportional to temperature. No NaN positions allowed. Particle count must match difficulty level (Easy=30, Medium=60, Hard=90). Focus score clamped 0-100. Temperature clamped 0.1-3.0. Mean orbital radius must stay between 2.0 and 5.0.
